note: 69 zones total, split between 55 Yellow Zone and 14 Boro Zone. Yellow Zone is the traditional street-hail area — most rider questions about being refused a hail or a driver not knowing a cross-street come from here. The 14 Boro Zone pockets (upper Manhattan edges) behave more like the outer boroughs for pickup patterns.

61 zones, all classified Boro Zone — no Yellow Zone coverage at all. Pickups here are overwhelmingly app-dispatched rather than street hails, so a rider complaint about 'the driver couldn't find me' is more often a pin-drop/address issue than a hail dispute.

69 zones. 67 are Boro Zone, and the other 2 are JFK Airport and LaGuardia Airport, both classified Airports — a distinct service zone from the rest of the borough. Airport-zone trips have different fare rules (flat-rate/surcharge questions) than the other 67 Queens zones, so route those complaints differently from a routine Boro Zone one.
43 zones, all Boro Zone. No airport or Yellow Zone coverage. Fare and pickup-pattern questions here should be handled the same way as Brooklyn and Staten Island, not Manhattan.

20 zones, all Boro Zone — the smallest zone count of the five boroughs. Lowest trip volume in the dataset; a rep seeing very few historical trips for a Staten Island zone shouldn't assume something's broken, that's the normal baseline here.
